newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS EASES OFF THROTTLE TO REACH FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS EASES OFF THROTTLE TO REACH FINAL.

text.p: Big hitting Australian Mark Philippoussis fought back from a set down to beat Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden at Queen's on Saturday and said he turned the match by slowing down his mighty serve.

The 20-year-old son of a former Melbourne taxi driver, who holds the record for the fastest recorded serve in tennis at 229 kph, struggled against Bjorkman's whipping returns before winning 2-6 7-6 6-2.
"Jonas has one of the best returns in the game. It's hard when it comes back as fast as you serve it," the 1.95-metre tall Australian said.
"So I thought maybe I'd slow the serve down and he started missing," Philippoussis, seeded six here, added.

In chilly conditions in west London, Philippoussis looked stiff and cold at the start of the match. He missed too many first serves and Bjorkman, who put out top seed and world number one Pete Sampras on Friday, took full advantage.
The 25-year-old eighth seed broke the Australian's shaky serve in the fifth and seventh games of the first set and in the first game of the second.

Bjorkman, a member of the Swedish Davis Cup squad and doubles winner here three years ago, slipped up in the fourth game of the second, losing his serve to some fine returns as the Australian warmed up and began to move more easily about the court.
Philippoussis won the tie-break 7-5, taking the set with a huge serve that Bjorkman flicked feebly into the net.
That set the tone for the rest of the match. Philippoussis went on to break the Swede's serve twice in the final set, serving 13 aces in total and bringing his tally for the tournament so far to 76.

The second semifinal at Queen's, a key warm-up tournament before Wimbledon starts on June 23, also features two big servers in third-seeded Croat Goran Ivanisevic and Britain's 16th seed Greg Rusedski.
